q: The capacitors are connected in ____ each capacitor has the same charge. (2024)
e: In a series connection of capacitors, the same charge accumulates on each capacitor.

q: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is ____. (2024)
e: The standard SI unit for measuring capacitance is the farad (F).

q: ____ is required to control the current and facilitate gradual charging or discharging in a capacitor circuit. (2024)
e: A resistor regulates the flow of current, allowing controlled charging or discharging of a capacitor.

q: In the series connection of the capacitors, each capacitor has the same ____. (2025)
e: Capacitors connected in series hold equal electric charge across their plates.

q: The SI unit of capacitance is ____. (2025)
e: In the SI system, capacitance is expressed in farads (F).

q: Electrolytic capacitors use the oxide layer as the ____ material. (2026)
e: In electrolytic capacitors, a thin layer of oxide functions as the dielectric medium.

q: The energy stored by the capacitor is W = ____. (2025, 2026)
e: The potential energy stored in a capacitor can be calculated using these equivalent formulas.

q: The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called ____ of a capacitor charging or discharging process. (2024)
e: The product RC gives the time constant, which characterizes the speed of charging or discharging.

q: Film capacitors use ____ film as the dielectric medium. (2024)
e: Film capacitors utilize a thin plastic film as an effective dielectric layer.

q: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1 V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is ____. (2025)
e: Capacitance C = Q / V, so 1 Coulomb at 1 Volt equals 1 Farad.

q: In practice, typical devices have capacitances ranging from ____. (2025)
e: Standard practical capacitors usually range in value from microfarads down to picofarads.

q: Electrolytic capacitor has a wide ____ capacity. (2025)
e: Electrolytic capacitors generally possess a broad tolerance range in capacitance manufacturing.

q: The final current is equal to ____ when the capacitor is fully charged. (2025)
e: When fully charged, the capacitor opposes the voltage source and current drops to zero.

q: The energy stored in a capacitor is directly proportional to the square of the ____ across its plates. (2025)
e: Energy stored is given by W = 1/2 C V^2, which depends on the square of the voltage.

q: The dielectric may be able to withstand a ____ electric field between the plates than air. (2025)
e: Dielectric materials can endure higher electric field strengths before experiencing breakdown compared to air.

q: ____ capacitors are used in radio tuning applications. (2025)
e: Variable capacitors allow manual tuning of capacitance to align radio receiver frequencies.

q: The ability of a capacitor to store an electric charge is measured in ____. (2025)
e: Capacitance is defined as the measure of electric charge stored per unit potential difference.

q: The formula that represents the energy stored in a capacitor is ____. (2025)
e: These standard equations express the energy stored in the electric field of a capacitor.

q: The equivalent unit of farad is ____. (2025)
e: From C = Q / V, one Farad equals one Coulomb per Volt.

q: The dielectric constant of vacuum or air is taken as ____. (2025)
e: The relative permittivity (dielectric constant) of air or vacuum is defined as 1.

q: The capacitor was originally known as a ____. (2025)
e: Historically, early capacitive storage devices were called condensers.

q: The capacitor is similar to a ____ battery. (2025)
e: A capacitor stores electrical energy temporarily and releases it rapidly, akin to a rechargeable battery.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor depends on the nature of the ____ between the two conductors. (2025)
e: The dielectric material placed between the plates affects how much charge the capacitor can store.

q: A capacitor stores ____ energy in the form of an electric field. (2025)
e: Capacitors store potential energy as an electric field established between their plates.

q: The working voltage of the film capacitors are up to ____ V. (2025)
e: Film capacitors can be designed to withstand high working voltages up to 1500 V.

q: The charge of a capacitor is directly proportional to its ____. (2025)
e: Charge Q is directly proportional to the potential difference V across the plates (Q = CV).

q: For a vacuum κ = 1 and for other media ____. (2025)
e: Dielectric materials other than a vacuum increase capacitance, so their dielectric constant k > 1.

q: The capacitors are connected in series each capacitor has the ____ charge. (2025)
e: In series arrangements, every capacitor acquires the exact same amount of electric charge.

q: Variable capacitors mostly use air as the ____ medium. (2026)
e: Air is commonly used as the dielectric in variable capacitors due to low loss at radio frequencies.

q: The equivalent capacitance of the capacitors connected in ____ is the sum of the capacitances of the individual capacitors. (2026)
e: When connected in parallel, individual capacitances add up directly to give equivalent capacitance.

q: The electrical energy W stored in the capacitor is given, in terms of charge Q and potential difference V, by ____. (2026)
e: In terms of Q and V, the stored electrical energy equation is W = 1/2 QV.

q: Placing a resistor in the charging circuit ____ the charging process. (2026)
e: Resistors restrict current flow, increasing the time constant and slowing down the charging process.
